Result: 12 passed, 0 failed (11 history tests plus one existing config test that matched the filter).

criteria.evidence: Athena's records for this tree: `cargo fmt --all --check` passed, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` passed, `cargo test --locked` passed with 1020 tests. The diff touches records.rs only to add two doc-comment lines, and no existing test code changed.

criteria.criterion: Public new items carry doc comments citing docs/design/records-history.md (§5.3, §4 or §8 as relevant) and D111. Fields follow the design: landing-intent has PR number, head sha, head tree sha, expected base, job ids; landing has PR number, head sha, host commit, merge method, ordered commits (sha, tree) with job and verification, and the intent it fulfills; intervention has declarer, reason and commit sha; import-manifest has C0 and per-path blob id and SHA-256; legacy-exempt has entries with sha and reason.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: the module doc cites docs/design/records-history.md and D111, and each pub struct or enum doc cites its section (§5.3, §4, §8/§9) and D111. Methods and fields have plain doc comments. The field sets match design lines 171-177 and 97: LandingIntent has pr_number, head_sha, head_tree_sha, expected_base, job_ids. Landing has pr_number, head_sha, host_commit, merge_method, commits[sha, tree, job, verification], intent. DeclaredIntervention has declarer, reason, commit_sha. ImportManifest has c0 and paths[path, blob_id, sha256]. LegacyExempt has entries[sha, reason].

summary: The change does what the accepted reading asks. It adds a new `athena-data::history` module with the six record types (landing-intent, landing, a declared intervention tagged `athena.declared-intervention/1`, checkpoint, legacy-exempt, import-manifest). Each type has a schema tag, rejects unknown fields and has a `validate` method, and the module carries tests for round-trips and rejections. I ran `cargo test -p athena-data history` on this snapshot: all 11 new tests passed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks (1020 tests) also passed. I checked the fields against §5.3 and §4 of docs/design/records-history.md and they match. The only edits outside the new module are a doc-comment line in records.rs, the module line in lib.rs, and the CHANGELOG entry. The diff adds no writer, no host-rules check, no git or branch code, and touches no other crate. The user's narrowed reading excludes the writer and the host-rules check, so their absence is not a gap. Cargo.toml was listed as a deliverable but did not change, which is fine because no new dependency was needed.
